What is the space efficiency difference between Cellular Automations with just 1 state per cell, versus those with no states and simple contracting rules?
I'm assuming we aren't looking for the third-order of magnitude difference (though all of those could probably be easily just about accommodated a within a hundred-ish words or so).
There's a slowly-recovering-some-paradigm-attempt to do so.
How many people, at some future point, on average, need to be reading Shakespeare's plays in order to have one in every room along their path home?
I'd look at Qab.
Would requiring such things  be a crime against humanity? Not if just making books effectively indefinable would be a crime against humanity.
Whole words might be simple enough, however, of course since working out what, say,  "progin "a"tim bad" read would end up being one of the gimmicks of a polynomial/polytime solver, the claimed save would be nil-er.
We can make interesting uses of that, a veritably new welcome, I've been thinking. ↶
What is the space efficiency difference between the Complete Graph with one edge between each pair of nodes and the Partial Graph with an edge weight between each pair of nodes subject to some constraint on those edges?
This is different from the previous question, for only some but not all pairs of nodes are connected.
